tools.name: isochrone_compute
tools.description: Returns a GeoJSON polygon covering everywhere reachable from an origin within a single cost budget. One endpoint serves both products — the `cost_type` field in the body selects which: | Cost Type | Product | Cost Value Unit | Question answered | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `time` | IsoChrone | seconds | 'How far can I get in 10 minutes?' | | `distance` | IsoDistance | metres | 'How far can I get within 5 km of road travel?' | Everything else — request shape, validation, response shape, error codes — is identical between the two modes. The response echoes the mode back in `features[0].properties.cost_type`. `direction` flips the direction of travel: `outbound` (default) is where you can reach from the origin; `inbound` is who can reach the origin. The two differ on one-ways, restricted turns and time-dependent costing. Exactly one contour is requested per call, so the response always contains exactly one feature. **SERVICE LIMITS** | Cost Type | Unit | Min (exclusive) | Max | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `time` | seconds | 0 | 7,200 | | `distance` | metres | 0 | 100,000 | | Travel Mode | Supported | | --- | --- | | auto | Yes | | motorcycle | Yes | | truck | Yes | | pedestrian | Yes | `cost_value` must satisfy `0 < cost_value <= max`. A value of `0`, a negative value, or a value above the max returns HTTP 400. A larger `cost_value` explores a larger area and costs more latency; the max caps worst-case compute time. The origin must lie inside the India boundary. **RESPONSE GEOMETRY FORMAT** By default, or when `encode_geojson` is omitted, the response uses encoded polyline strings to reduce response size. If you want standard GeoJSON coordinates directly, send `encode_geojson: false`. | `encode_geojson` | Response geometry | | --- | --- | | omitted or `true` (default) | Encoded polyline strings | | `false` | Standard GeoJSON numeric coordinate arrays in `[longitude, latitude]` order |. Required: cost_type, cost_value, origin. Optional: departure_time, direction (default: outbound), enable_smoothing (default: false) (plus 6 more).

params.name: cost_type
params.description: Selects the product: `time` → isochrone (budget in seconds), `distance` → isodistance (budget in metres).

params.name: cost_value
params.description: The budget. Seconds when `cost_type` is `time` (max 7,200 = 120 min); metres when `cost_type` is `distance` (max 100,000 = 100 km). Must be greater than 0.

params.name: departure_time
params.description: Departure time in IST, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`. Only used when `traffic_aware` is `true`.

params.name: direction
params.description: `outbound` = area reachable from the origin; `inbound` = area that can reach the origin.

params.name: enable_smoothing
params.description: Reserved. Accepted and type-validated, but currently has no effect on the returned geometry.

params.name: encode_geojson
params.description: Response geometry format. The default is `true` when this field is omitted, which returns encoded geometry to reduce response size. Set to `false` to receive standard GeoJSON numeric coordinate arrays in `[longitude, latitude]` order. This changes only the response representation, not the computed reachable area.

params.name: origin
params.description: Origin point as `[latitude, longitude]`. Must be inside India.

params.name: req_id
params.description: Optional client correlation id — echoed back in the response and recorded in logs.

params.name: resolution
params.description: Polygon detail. `high` returns more vertices and a tighter boundary at a small latency cost; `low` returns a coarser, lighter polygon.

params.name: route-modifiers-avoid-highways
params.description: Penalise highways.

params.name: route-modifiers-avoid-tolls
params.description: Penalise tolled roads.

params.name: traffic_aware
params.description: Enables time-dependent costing for `cost_type: time`.

params.name: travel_mode
params.description: Vehicle profile used for the expansion.

tools.name: matrix_compute
tools.description: Computes distance (km) and duration (seconds) for every source→target pair. Returns a 2D matrix indexed as `[source_index][target_index]`. **SERVICE LIMITS** | Travel Mode | Max Location Pairs | Max Distance | | --- | --- | --- | | auto | 40,000 | 6,000 km | | motorcycle | 40,000 | 6,000 km | | truck | 40,000 | 6,000 km | | pedestrian | 40,000 | 200 km |. Required: sources, targets. Optional: route_modifiers, travel_mode (default: auto).

params.name: route-modifiers-avoid-highways
params.description: Avoid highways

params.name: route-modifiers-avoid-tolls
params.description: Avoid tolls

params.name: sources
params.description: List of `[lat, lng]` source coordinates. All within India.

params.name: targets

params.name: travel_mode
params.description: Travel mode

params.name: size
params.description: Tile pixel dimensions (256 or 512).

params.name: z

params.name: x

tools.name: route_compute
tools.description: Calculates the optimal route between 2+ waypoints within India. Supports multiple travel modes, alternate routes, and route modifiers. **BREAKING CHANGE (v4.7):** Geometry is now **encoded** by default. Unless you send `output_format: { 'encode_polyline': false }`, both `geometry` and every `legs[].shape` are returned as encoded polyline strings (precision 6). Maneuvers are **off** by default — send `output_format: { 'maneuvers': true }` to include them. The old `decode_geometry` query parameter has been removed; use `output_format.encode_polyline` in the request body instead. **SERVICE LIMITS** | Travel Mode | Max Locations | | --- | --- | | auto | 20 | | motorcycle | 50 | | truck | 20 | | pedestrian | 50 | Requests exceeding the max location count return HTTP 400. There is no pre-check for maximum distance. Required: geo_coords. Optional: alternate_routes (default: false), departure_time, output_format (plus 3 more). Returns array of RouteComputeItem.

params.name: alternate_routes
params.description: Include alternate routes in response.

params.name: departure_time
params.description: Specifies the planned departure time (for example, `2026-06-03T18:00`) in ISO-8601 format. Defaults to the current time. This parameter is considered only when `traffic_aware` is set to `true`.

params.name: geo_coords
params.description: Ordered `[lat, lng]` waypoints. Minimum 2, all within India.

params.name: output-format-encode-polyline
params.description: `true` → `geometry` and each `legs[].shape` are encoded polyline strings (precision 6). `false` → both are decoded `[[lat, lng], ...]` point lists. Replaces the old `decode_geometry` query parameter.

params.name: output-format-maneuvers
params.description: `false` → the `maneuvers` key is absent from every leg. `true` → each leg includes a `maneuvers` array (with `bearing_after`, `bearing_before`, `cost`, `travel_type`, `travel_mode`, and `time` removed from each maneuver).

params.name: route-modifiers-avoid-highways
params.description: Avoid highways

params.name: route-modifiers-avoid-tolls
params.description: Avoid tolls

params.name: traffic_aware
params.description: Enables hour-of-day traffic-aware ETA calculations.

params.name: travel_mode
params.description: One of auto, motorcycle, truck, pedestrian.

tools.name: route-plan_plan-routes
tools.description: Solves the Vehicle Routing Problem (VRP) by assigning delivery orders across a fleet of vehicles from a central depot to generate optimized, stop-by-stop routes. Accepts location data as exact coordinates or text addresses with automatic geocoding. The engine minimizes total transit distance and duration while enforcing per-vehicle weight and volume limits. **ORDER LOCATION** Each order must specify either a order coordinate pair (`lat, long`) or an order address. If an address is provided, it is automatically geocoded, and the resolved coordinates are returned in the resulting route stop payload. **SERVICE LIMITS** | Constraint | Description | | --- | --- | | Orders | Must be between 1 and 50. | | Order Address | Order address must be located in India. | | Order Location | Order Location must be within Indian territory. |. Required: depot_lat, depot_lng, num_vehicles, orders. Optional: max_distance, max_stops, max_time (plus 5 more). Returns the new PlanResponse.

params.name: depot_lat
params.description: Depot latitude.

params.name: depot_lng
params.description: Depot longitude.

params.name: max_distance
params.description: Maximum distance in kilometers till which the vehicle can be used. Defaults to 1000 km.

params.name: max_stops
params.description: Maximum number of unique locations a vehicle can visit in a route apart from its starting location. Defaults to 100.

params.name: max_time
params.description: Maximum time in seconds till which the vehicle can be used. Defaults to 86400 seconds (1 day).

params.name: num_vehicles
params.description: Number of vehicles available at the depot.

params.name: orders
params.description: A list of dictionaries where each dictionary contains the metadata of an order.

params.name: plan_start_time
params.description: Absolute wall-clock time at which the vehicle shift begins (e.g., '2026-06-03 09:00+05:30'). If missing, order time windows are dropped.

params.name: return_to_depot
params.description: Controls whether vehicles must return to the depot after serving their last order.

params.name: vehicle_max_volume
params.description: Maximum volume in cubic centimeters that one vehicle in this contract can serve. Defaults to 100000 cm³.

params.name: vehicle_max_weight
params.description: Maximum weight in kilograms that one vehicle in this contract can serve. Defaults to 1000 kg.

params.name: vehicle_mode
params.description: Travel mode passed through to the distance-matrix API. Allowed values: 'auto', 'truck', 'bike', 'foot'.

tools.name: toll-charges-by-od_toll_charges_by_od
tools.description: Calculates toll charges for a journey between an origin and destination coordinate pair. The system computes the route internally and identifies toll plazas along the route. Supports multiple vehicle types and optionally returns alternate routes with their toll breakdowns. **SERVICE LIMITS** | Constraint | Value | | --- | --- | | Waypoints | Optional ordered intermediate stops between origin & destination | | Vehicle types | `motorcycle`, `car_jeep_van`, `lcv`, `bus_truck`, `upto_3_axle`, `axle_4_to_6`, `hcm_eme`, `axle_7_plus` | | Max routes returned | 1 recommended + alternates | > When `waypoints` are supplied, the routing engine returns a single stitched route (no alternates), regardless of `include_alternates`. Required: destination, origin, vehicle_type. Optional: include_alternates (default: true), include_polyline (default: false), req_id (plus 1 more).

params.name: destination-lat

params.name: destination-lng

params.name: include_alternates
params.description: If true, returns toll breakdowns for alternate routes in addition to the recommended route. Ignored when waypoints are supplied.

params.name: include_polyline

params.name: origin-lat

Required: routes, vehicle_type. Optional: req_id. Returns the new TollByRouteResponse.

tools.name: verify_address

Address validation runs first — the history lookup only proceeds on a valid, premise-level match. `is_verified=false` can mean: address could not be resolved, no delivery recorded in the window, address not specific enough (PREMISE level required), or no delivery records found at this location. **SERVICE LIMITS** | Parameter | Range | | --- | --- | | `months` min | 1 | | `months` max | 24 |. Required: address, months. Optional: req_id. Returns the new VerifyAddressResponse.

params.name: address
params.description: Raw delivery address to verify

params.name: months
params.description: Lookback window in months. Checks if address was delivered to within this period.

novel_features.name: Bulk address cleaning
novel_features.description: Clean a CSV of raw addresses into standardised, validated, geocoded rows: up to 3 calls per uncached address (about 16 a day per token); overflow rows are marked deferred.

novel_features.name: Trip quote
novel_features.description: Get distance, traffic ETA and toll plazas for a trip in one record. Costs up to 4 calls per lane (geocode from and to, route, toll).

novel_features.name: Service-area coverage check
novel_features.description: Flag orders that fall outside a hub's 45-minute (or N km) service area. Costs 1 isochrone call plus 1 call per uncached address.

novel_features.name: Fleet plan from orders file
novel_features.description: Turn an orders file of addresses or coordinates into per-vehicle stop sequences. Costs 1 call per 50 orders from a separate 5-per-day route-plan pool; about 30s each.

novel_features.name: Cached-address quality report
novel_features.description: See address quality and granularity broken down by pincode or city across everything you have cleaned. Local-only and free; empty until address clean has run.

novel_features.name: Duplicate-doorstep finder
novel_features.description: Find repeated delivery locations among addresses you have cleaned. Local-only and free; empty until address clean has run.
